model_organism.citation: Lee et al. 2018 - NGL-2 Deletion Leads to Autistic-like Behaviors Responsive to NMDAR Modulation (PMID: 29949768)
phenotypes: Suppressed NMDAR-dependent synaptic plasticity in the hippocampus
Mild social interaction deficits
Repetitive behaviors
Autistic-like behaviors rapidly improved by pharmacological NMDAR activation
NGL-2 associates with NMDARs via PSD-95-dependent and -independent mechanisms

model_organism.citation: 2025 - LRRC4 enhances synaptic function and alleviates neuronal injury in high-fat diet mice (PMID: 41494607)
phenotypes: Impaired synaptic plasticity
Cognitive impairment (Morris water maze, nest building)
Further decreased PSD-95 expression in HFD-fed Lrrc4-/- mice
Decreased Bcl-2 and increased cleaved caspase-3 and BAX in hippocampus of HFD Lrrc4-/- mice
Exacerbated neuronal injury and apoptosis
Overexpression of LRRC4 rescued behavioral abnormalities, increased dendritic branching, and strengthened synaptic transmission in HFD mice

model_organism.citation: 2021 - LRRC4 functions as a neuron-protective role in experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (PMID: 33932995)
phenotypes: Accelerated and exacerbated EAE disease progression
More severe myelin degeneration in the spinal cord
Increased leukocyte infiltration into the spinal cord
Elevated Rab7b and NF-κB p65
Increased IL-6 and IFN-γ, decreased TNF-α
Stronger Th1 immune response
AAV-LRRC4 expression alleviated EAE symptoms and protected neurons

model_organism.citation: 2023 - Whole genome sequencing identifies genetic variants associated with neurogenic inflammation in rosacea (PMID: 37402769)
phenotypes: Knock-in of a recurrent human Lrrc4 mutation causes rosacea-like skin inflammation
Excessive vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP) release by peripheral neurons

biological.citation: LRRC4 Deficiency Drives Premature Ovarian Insufficiency by Disrupting Metabolic Homeostasis in Granulosa Cells (PMID: 40317712)
biological.summary: LRRC4 is expressed in ovarian granulosa cells and supports folliculogenesis and ovarian reserve. LRRC4 deficiency causes defective oocyte maturation, follicular atresia and POI. LRRC4 promotes K48-linked ubiquitin degradation of YAP, which balances mitochondrial fission/fusion, limits mitophagy and maintains aerobic respiration/glycolysis. Targeting LRRC4 normalized follicular development in POI model mice.

biological.citation: LRRC4 mediates the formation of circular RNA CD44 to inhibit GBM cell proliferation (PMID: 34631278)
biological.summary: LRRC4 interacts with the RNA-binding protein SAM68 and blocks SAM68 binding to CD44 pre-mRNA, which promotes circCD44 biogenesis. circCD44 sponges miR-326 and miR-330-5p to regulate SMAD6, defining an LRRC4/SAM68/circCD44/miR-326/miR-330-5p/SMAD6 axis. circCD44 re-expression suppressed GBM proliferation, colony formation, invasion and in vivo tumor growth.

biological.citation: LRRC4 Suppresses E-Cadherin-Dependent Collective Cell Invasion and Metastasis in Epithelial Ovarian Cancer (PMID: 32117780)
biological.summary: LRRC4 binds the cSH2 domain of PIK3R1 and inhibits PIK3R1 activity without disrupting PIK3R1–PIK3CA binding. This inhibits AKT/GSK3β/β-catenin signaling and E-cadherin-dependent collective invasion and metastasis. LRRC4 is low in HGSC and metastasis, and AAV9-LRRC4 reduced metastasis in an orthotopic xenograft model.

biological.citation: LRRC4 functions as a neuron-protective role in experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (PMID: 33932995)
biological.summary: LRRC4 is mainly expressed in spinal cord neurons and is decreased in EAE mice. LRRC4-/- mice had worse EAE, with more demyelination, leukocyte infiltration and a stronger Th1 response. Loss of LRRC4 raised Rab7b and NF-κB p65, and AAV-LRRC4 overexpression alleviated disease.

biological.citation: Expression and functional characterization of LRRC4, a novel brain-specific member of the LRR superfamily (PMID: 15967442)
biological.summary: LRRC4 expression is restricted to normal adult brain in human and mouse, is developmentally regulated, and is down-regulated in brain tumors and U251MG cells. Induction in a Tet-on system caused late G1 delay, with changes in p21, p27, Cdk2, PCNA and p-ERK1/2.

biological.citation: Expression and clinical significance of LRRC4 in benign and malignant nasopharyngeal diseases (PMID: 26662436)
biological.summary: By immunohistochemistry, LRRC4 was strongly expressed in chronic nasopharyngitis (82.1%) and precancerous lesions (81.8%) but weakly in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (10%). Loss of LRRC4 expression is a major feature of NPC and did not differ by stage or grade.

biological.citation: LRRC4 inhibits glioma cell growth and invasion through a miR-185-dependent pathway (PMID: 22834685)
biological.summary: LRRC4 upregulates miR-185, which targets CDC42 and RhoA (with indirect effects on VEGFA), to suppress glioma cell invasion. Low LRRC4 and miR-185 correlate with poor glioma patient outcome.

biological.citation: LRRC4 inhibits glioblastoma cell proliferation, migration, and angiogenesis by downregulating pleiotropic cytokine expression and responses (PMID: 17541939)
biological.summary: Stable LRRC4 expression in U251 cells reduced cytokines and their receptors, K-RAS expression, and phosphorylation of c-Raf, ERK, AKT, NF-κBp65, p70S6K and PKC. It also reduced AP-1, NF-κB and CyclinD1 activation, indicating inhibition of RTK signaling. LRRC4 blunted cytokine-driven proliferation and migration and impaired VEGF-induced endothelial tube formation.

biological.citation: MicroRNA-381 Favors Repair of Nerve Injury Through Regulation of the SDF-1/CXCR4 Signaling Pathway via LRRC4 in Acute Cerebral Ischemia after Cerebral Lymphatic Blockage (PMID: 29669322)
biological.summary: LRRC4 is a target of miR-381 in a rat MCAO/cerebral lymphatic blockage model. miR-381 upregulation lowers LRRC4 and activates SDF-1/CXCR4 signaling (with increased pERK, Slit2, VEGF). This reduced infarct volume, apoptosis and inflammation and promoted nerve repair.

biological.citation: LRRC4 Orchestrates AP2A1-Containing Clathrin-Coated Vesicles to Disrupt Mitochondrial Cristae and Restrict Glioblastoma Progression (PMID: 42439431)
biological.summary: LRRC4 is a Golgi-anchored tumor suppressor that engages AP2A1-containing clathrin-coated vesicles and redirects them to the inner mitochondrial membrane. This disrupts the MICOS complex, suppresses Mic60, collapses cristae, impairs oxidative phosphorylation and triggers excessive mitophagy. The result is suppressed GBM proliferation and invasion in vitro and in xenografts.
